feedback: Approved for the final race, unchanged. The candidate is the iteration 8 design (y 0.065 m, x -0.07 to 0.07, sensor_size 0.016, kp 2.6, kd 0.6, ki 0.1, base_speed 1.2, last_direction). It is the best raced design so far (431.06 in iteration 8), and its oval was 20/20 finishes at mean 944 with max_error 0.0334. Iteration 9 (base_speed 1.1) scored 425.05 and iteration 10 (kd 0.5) scored 427.56. Both left the s-bend and slalom off track, so neither beat iteration 8. Iterations 5 to 7 showed that moving the sensor row to y 0.03 or shrinking sensor_size to 0.012 lowers the score, so those directions are closed. No iterations remain after this one, and the unseen-track race is scored only on this build. Nothing further can be tested, so the remaining question is whether this design generalises. The unseen track may be a different shape, so the main risk is off-track endings on tight bends, as seen on the s-bend and slalom. This is not a prediction of the result. Do not revise the controller or geometry: the untested changes available (base_speed 1.1 or 1.3, kd 0.5 at y 0.065) were already raced and did not beat iteration 8.
requested_changes: Keep geometry and controller exactly as submitted: sensor y 0.065 m, x -0.07 to 0.07, sensor_size 0.016, kp 2.6, ki 0.1, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.2, line_loss last_direction. Iteration 8 is the best raced score (431.06).
Do not switch to kd 0.5 or base_speed 1.1 for the final race. Iteration 10 (kd 0.5) scored 427.56 and iteration 9 (base_speed 1.1) scored 425.05, both below iteration 8.
Do not move sensor y back to 0.05 or to 0.03, and do not use sensor_size 0.012. Iterations 5 (403.4), 7 (199.7) and 6 (302.6) all scored lower than iteration 8.
